thread.title: Apple, Facebook, Nvidia Lead Tech Stocks As Market Rallies

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple, Facebook, Nvidia Lead Tech Stocks As Market Rallies

organizations.name: nvidia lead tech stocks as market rallies tech

text:
Tech stocks led Tuesday's market rally, which was fueled by easing trade war fears following China President Xi Jinping's pro-globalization remarks .
X PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) leapt 2.2%, SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) rallied 1.8%,and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) advanced 1.6% in the stock market today . DowDuPont ( DWDP ), Intel ( INTC ) and Boeing ( BA ) were among seven Dow stocks rising more than 3% each.
Apple ( AAPL ) added 2.1% to regain its 50-day moving average, which it gave up Monday. Shares of the iPhone maker have been hitting resistance at that line the past three weeks. They have held above the 200-day line during that time.
Facebook ( FB ) gained 4.2% as CEO Mark Zuckerberg testified before a Senate Committee regarding the data scandal. Shares remain below their 200-day line and are 15% off their high.
Energy, semiconductors and biotechs were among the biggest sector fund gainers Tuesday, while utilities and real estate lagged. VanEck Vectors Oil Services ( OIH ) surged nearly 6% to retake its 50-day line for the first time in over two months. West Texas intermediate crude prices soared 4% to $65.79 a barrel.
SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ( XOP ) gained 4.5% and Energy Select Sector SPDR ( XLE ) added 3.6%.
Graphics chip designer and artificial intelligence player Nvidia ( NVDA ) vaulted nearly 6% on an upgrade from Morgan Stanley to overweight from equal weight. It's now 4% below its 50-day moving average and 10% off its 52-week high.
Defensive Play Given the market's volatility, most U.S. stock funds are testing support near their 200-day moving average.
So it stands to reason that a commodity-based safe-haven play is faring better. SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ), which tracks the price of gold, remains above its 50-day moving average . Shares may be forming a flat base with a potential buy point at 129.61. GLD was last featured in this ETF column on March 29 as it sought support at the 50-day line.
The $36.8 billion fund extended its year-to-date gain to 2.6% as of Monday, according to Morningstar Inc. The S&P 500, meantime, pulled back 2.3%. But the gold ETF's average annual returns over the past three, five and 10 years sharply lag the S&P 500's performance over those same periods.
GLD carries a 0.40% expense ratio. Younger peer iShares Gold Trust ( IAU ), which bears a 0.25% expense ratio, shows similar price action to GLD.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The $11.8 billion iShares fund, which marked its 13th anniversary in January, also returned 2.6% through Monday. Its average annual returns over the past three, five and 10 years also underperformed the S&P 500 by a wide margin.
The increased volatility in the stock market as the U.S. and China try to slap tariffs on each other's goods, heightening concerns about a potential trade war, could be considered "short-term noise," U.S. Global Investors CEO Frank Holmes wrote in a Monday blog post . Other news shaking up the market include Facebook ( FB ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), he notes, which could face close regulatory scrutiny.
Gold Haven? "Although U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports, and China's proposed taxes on American goods, have not been imposed yet, markets are already beginning to price in the news," Holmes wrote. "A trade war could be a concern sometime down the road, but I'm confident U.S. and Chinese officials can work together to avert a full-blown tit-for-tat standoff."
However, due to some early warnings sings of possible economic turbulence ahead, Holmes says: "I would highly urge investors to ensure a portion of their portfolio is in a historically reliable store of value—investment-grade municipal bonds, for instance, and gold bullion and gold mining stocks."
